title: Canyon Aeroad CFR First Ride Review - The Ultimate Aero Race Bike?

takeaways.text: Canyon claims more stiffness in key areas, a slimmer head tube and down tube, a deeper fork and a new seat tube and clamp (moved to the top tube) after the previous generation's seatpost failures.

The one-piece PACE bar is height-adjustable without cutting the steerer, has removable drops in several widths, and optional aero drops claimed to save 14 W; the Gear Groove mount accepts computers or clip-on bars.
Clearance is 32 mm with 28 mm tires fitted, and the fork has rubber feet to rest on when the wheel is out.
His size-M SRAM Red CFR with Zipp 454 wheels weighed 7.1 kg; that build cost just under £9,800.
It feels almost identical to the previous Aeroad, faster than a Tarmac SL8 in his testing and smoother on rough tarmac than earlier aero bikes, though not as supple as a Tarmac SL8 or Madone SLR.
The carbon bottle cages hold Canyon's own bottles snugly, but other bottles rattle and can fall out.

disclosure: How the test bike was supplied is not stated in the video; the build shown is the SRAM Red Aeroad CFR rather than the candidate's Dura-Ace Di2 build.
summary: First ride on the fourth-generation (2024) Canyon Aeroad CFR, covering frame changes, cockpit, clearance, weight and ride.
